main_body: small grey stone mortar bowl with green herbs inside and a brown pestle leaning out to the upper right
top_band: light grey rim (#c8d0d0) at row 8 on the left, then one green herb row (#2e8a2a) at row 9. At the centre column the rim is covered by the pestle and only the 1 green row shows. This is a thin 1-2 row ellipse, not a clear surface.
evidence: In the centre column (x=9) the pestle sits on rows 7-8, one green row at row 9, then the grey bowl wall in rows 10-13 (L 137, 103, 79, 79). The opening is only about 1 row of green plus a 1 row rim, which is too thin to read as an ellipse looking down into the bowl. The bowl reads mainly as a front-facing wall with a rim line and a little herb colour. There is no distinct front-edge line and no visible interior wall. This is a rim-only top on a container, so it fails the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The piece is smaller than one tile, so the per-tile measure is 0 and I judged by eye. The grey bowl has about 5 steps (#c8d0d0, #828a95, #606878, #49505d, #333942). The pestle has 3 browns and the herbs have 2-3 greens. Outline pixels are 0% neutral, so they carry a tint of the neighbouring material rather than being a black sticker line. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, with no 5x5 blocks of one colour. It has only 15 colours against 38-40 in the references, and the bowl wall is smooth with little grain or speckle. It is a little thinner than the references but acceptable for a tiny prop, so it passes.
